correctness.rationale: Direct derivation of residual path sum, exact parity sums, and unrestricted strict convexity: any two distinct positive exact-budget allocations differ in at least two coordinates, so every one-edge-outage reciprocal loss is strictly convex along their segment. Price-preserving automorphisms force two edge classes at unique optimum. Two branch derivatives yield both sharp thresholds and all boundary values; explicit formulas satisfy budget. The nominal comparison is a differentiable Lagrange necessary-condition argument. Standalone program passed 2,478 finite cross-checks including independent weighted Laplacian spectra; symbolic identities tested separately. Finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Single-link outages and total effective resistance are natural reliability design criteria. The theorem identifies a counterintuitive nonzero price interval where robust optimum equalizes unequal-price conductances, while nominal optimum cannot do so for any unequal prices. It gives a unique, unrestricted allocation formula, sharp reciprocal thresholds and a large-size width law, providing a meaningful exact benchmark for a known nonsmooth robust optimization framework rather than a routine unmotivated special value.
